core_obligations: Embed F and G into module-valued functors and form the diagonal embedding of F into the direct sum (proof lines 716-724).
Use the cokernel lemma to find a module map whose kernel is F (proof lines 725-728).
Exhibit Ker(phi) as the kernel of the map to the direct sum of that module and N (proof lines 729-730).
proof_roadmap: Embeddings and the diagonal square (proof lines 716-724).
difficulty_reason: For a ring A and a map phi : F -> G of adequate functors, the lemma asserts that the kernel of phi is adequate (statement lines 708-713). The proof embeds F and G into module-valued functors, forms the diagonal embedding of F into the direct sum so that the resulting square commutes, invokes the cokernel lemma to realise F as the kernel of an explicit map into a module-valued functor, and concludes by exhibiting Ker(phi) as the kernel of the map into the direct sum of that module and N (proof lines 715-730). The level is H3: the diagonal trick and the reduction to a kernel representation are both displayed, and the commuting square is drawn.
